figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. Distribution and biosynthesis of prenylated compounds in mulberry. a) Typical structures of prenylated compounds in mulberry. The prenyl
groups and the ortho electron-donating oxygen atoms are highlighted in red and cyan, respectively. b) The primary reaction sites and prenyl donors
of prenylation in the compounds of mulberry. *This substitution requires a ﬂavanone substrate with a hydroxy group at the C3 site. **This
substitution requires a ﬂavanone substrate with a hydroxy group at the C2 site. ***This substitution requires a moracin substrate with a hydroxy
group at the C5 site. P, G, and F denote the prenyl, geranyl, and farnesyl groups, respectively. c) Previously reported MaPTs and those identiﬁed in
this study. IDT, isoliquiritigenin 3′-dimethylallyltransferase; OGT, oxyresveratrol geranyltransferase.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. The analysis of phylogeny and gene expression level of MaPTs.
a) The phylogenetic tree of MaPTs and their paralogs of the UbiA family
in the M. alba genome. The tree was constructed using the
neighbor-joining algorithm with 1000 bootstrap replicates based on the
amino acid sequences encoded by these genes. The size of the node
circles is proportional to the bootstrap value. MaPT9 and MaPT11
correspond to the previously reported MaIDT and MaOGT, respectively.
ATG4, chlorophyll synthase; ABC4, 1,4-dihydroxy-2-napthoic acid
phytyltransferase; PPT1, p-hydroxybenzoate polyprenyltransferase;
COX10, heme O synthase; VTE2-1, homogentisate phytyltransferase;
VTE2-2, homogentisate solanesyltransferase. b) Heat map showing the
transcription levels of MaPTs in diﬀerent tissues of M. alba seedlings.
Transcription levels were derived from the RNA-Seq data we previously
published.[20] FR, ﬁbrous roots; TR, taproots; S, stems; CKL, untreated
leaves; UVL, ultraviolet-B treated leaves; BCL, Botrytis cinerea-infected
leaves.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. Prenylation of moracin M with DMAPP a) and GPP b) catalyzed by MaPTs. Microsomes from tobacco expressing EGFP were used as
negative controls to exclude interference from endogenous proteins. All chromatographic signals were acquired using a tunable UV detector at a
wavelength of 320 nm. All chromatograms in a) and b) share the same Y-axis scale, respectively. PM1-4: 7-prenylmoracin M, 2′-prenylmoracin M,
4′-prenylmoracin M, and 5-prenylmoracin M. GM1-4: 7-geranylmoracin M, 2′-geranylmoracin M, 4′-geranylmoracin M, and 5-geranylmoracin M.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4. The molecular basis of MaPT27 combining the prenyl donor. a) The overall and local view of the complex of protein, ligands, bilayer, and
solvent (water) after molecular simulation. Solvent molecules are shown as silver surface. b) Structure comparison of MaPT27, CgUBIAD1, and
AfUbiA. c) The closed substrate binding pocket of MaPT27. d) Binding conformation and interactions of MaPT27 with DMAPP and Mg2+.
e) Comparative analysis of residues involved in prenyl donor binding in MaPTs and their homologous proteins. Ae, Arnebia euchroma; Le,
Lithospermum erythrorhizon; Af, Archaeoglobus fulgidus; Ap, Aeropyrum pernix; Mj, Methanocaldococcus jannaschii; Cg, Cricetulus griseus. HG,
homogentisate; PHB, p-hydroxybenzoic acid. f) The catalytic activity of MaPT27 mutants toward moracin M and DMAPP substrates. The
chromatographic signals were acquired using a tunable UV detector at a wavelength of 320 nm, and all chromatograms share the same Y-axis scale.
PM1, 7-prenyl-moracin M; PM4, 5-prenyl-moracin M.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 5
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 5. Regioselective catalytic mechanism of MaPTs toward moracin M. a) The binding conformation and interactions among MaPT27, DMAPP,
and moracin M determined by MD simulation. b) The transition states (TS) of the reactions between moracin M and allylic cation at the C7 and C5
sites in the absence of enzymatic catalysis. c) The binding conformation and interactions among MaPT27, GPP, and moracin M determined by
ﬂexible docking. d) The binding conformation and interactions among MaPT29, DMAPP, and moracin M obtained by ﬂexible docking. e) The binding
conformation and interactions among MaPT21, DMAPP, and moracin M obtained by ﬂexible docking. f) Comparison of key residues that interacted
with moracin M in MaPT27 and MaPT29. g) Catalytic activity of wild-type and mutant MaPT27 proteins toward moracin M and DMAPP. In the protein
structure diagrams, the black, violet, and blue dashed lines represent hydrogen bonds, π–π stacking interactions, and the linear distances from the
C1 atom of DMAPP to the reaction sites on moracin M, respectively. All distances are measured in angstroms. All chromatograms share the same
Y-axis scale. PM1, 7-prenylmoracin M; PM4, 5-prenylmoracin M.
